papers.t: A randomized phase 2 study combining midostaurin, low-dose cytarabine and venetoclax in newly diagnosed AML ≥60 years
papers.c: Combining midostaurin with LV enhanced CRc among the sub-group of patients (n=29) with FLT3-ITD (82% vs 57%, difference = 25%, 0.85 posterior probability true difference > 5%, 95% CrI: -10 to 59%) and improved FLT3-ITD clearance as measured by ultrasensitive NGS (65% vs 0%), resulting in longer OS (median 24.2 vs 8.8 months, HR=0.34, 95% CrI: 0.071 to 0.960), compared to LV. In conclusion, midostaurin combined with low-dose cytarabine and venetoclax is well-tolerated and may have a role in newly diagnosed FLT3-ITD AML unfit for intensive chemotherapy.
ab: In randomized studies, addition of FLT3 inhibitors failed to improve survival in older patients with FLT3-ITD AML unfit for intensive chemotherapy. Although hypomethylating agents or low-dose cytarabine combined with venetoclax is standard, FLT3-ITD is an important mechanism of resistance and a barrier to improved survival. Recent studies show promise for the addition of gilteritinib or quizartinib to less intensive venetoclax-based therapy, however resulting marrow toxicity requires substantial reductions to administered treatment. The INTERVENE study (Investigating Novel Triplets to Extend Remission with VENetoclax in Elderly AML) (ACTRN12619001655134) examined the role of midostaurin (M) administered sequentially after low-dose cytarabine (L) combined with venetoclax (V) in patients with newly diagnosed AML ≥60 years with non-adverse karyotype. After a run-in phase (n=18) established that LDAC combined with venetoclax from days 1-28 and midostaurin from days 11-28 was tolerable, 120 patients were randomized 2:1 to receive either LVM or LV. For the primary endpoint, LVM did not improve composite complete remission (CRc), compared to LV (72% vs 68%). Combining midostaurin with LV enhanced CRc among the sub-group of patients (n=29) with FLT3-ITD (82% vs 57%, difference = 25%, 0.85 posterior probability true difference > 5%, 95% CrI: -10 to 59%) and improved FLT3-ITD clearance as measured by ultrasensitive NGS (65% vs 0%), resulting in longer OS (median 24.2 vs 8.8 months, HR=0.34, 95% CrI: 0.071 to 0.960), compared to LV. In conclusion, midostaurin combined with low-dose cytarabine and venetoclax is well-tolerated and may have a role in newly diagnosed FLT3-ITD AML unfit for intensive chemotherapy.

papers.t: The blind spots of post-transplant AML relapse: from clinical signal to mechanism-matched therapy
papers.c: We use TP53-mutated AML as an integrated case study of multi-mechanism failure. We conclude with practice points, a research agenda, and future considerations for the mechanism-defining studies required to make further progress.
ab: Relapse after allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation remains the dominant cause of death in acute myeloid leukaemia (AML), and outcomes after relapse remain poor despite substantial advances in supportive care, monitoring and therapy. Contemporary practice includes detailed monitoring and offers an expanding therapeutic toolkit including GVHD prophylaxis, engineered grafts, maintenance and targeted therapies. The biological understanding required to apply these tools selectively has, however, not kept pace. In this review we present an integrated clinical approach that connects the monitoring signal at impending relapse to the mechanism of graft-versus-leukaemia failure and the mechanism-matched therapeutic choice. We comprehensively review transplant care from conditioning through maintenance and relapse and highlight unresolved questions organised around graft versus host disease and graft versus leukaemia, fixed or reversible mechanisms of failure and maintenance therapies. We use TP53-mutated AML as an integrated case study of multi-mechanism failure. We conclude with practice points, a research agenda, and future considerations for the mechanism-defining studies required to make further progress.

papers.t: A Novel PICALM::AFF3 Fusion t(2;11) (q11.2;q21) in a Case of Myelodysplastic Neoplasm, Post Cytotoxic Therapy
Serine auxotrophy is a targetable vulnerability driven by PSAT1 suppression in AML
papers.c: We also found that SG restriction synergized with venetoclax in serine auxotrophic AML, and that MECOM rearrangement was strongly associated with PSAT1 suppression and serine auxotrophy. These findings define a metabolically distinct AML subtype and nominate it for targeting by SG restriction.
ab: Serine metabolism is of growing biologic and therapeutic interest in cancer. Upregulation of the serine synthesis pathway (SSP) can fuel tumor growth, and cancers with this phenotype are often sensitive to. SSP inhibitors. In parallel, dietary restriction of serine and glycine (SG) can suppress some cancers, but the determinants of sensitivity to. this approach are poorly understood. This is especially true in acute myeloid leukemia (AML), where serine metabolism has been less explored. We report that a subset of human AML cell lines and primary samples are completely dependent on external serine, known as serine auxotrophy. These leukemias consistently suppressed the SSP enzyme PSAT1, failed to. synthesize serine, responded to. SG restriction in vivo, and were rescued by restoring PSAT1. We also found that SG restriction synergized with venetoclax in serine auxotrophic AML, and that MECOM rearrangement was strongly associated with PSAT1 suppression and serine auxotrophy. These findings define a metabolically distinct AML subtype and nominate it for targeting by SG restriction.

papers.t: Risk Factors for Admission to the Intensive Care Unit and Mortality in Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplant Recipients with Acute Myeloid Leukemia
papers.c: Together, these results highlight that ICU admission is common after allografting in adults with AML and is associated with high mortality. Identification of patients at increased risk may, ultimately, help develop possible preventive strategies and allow testing in particularly vulnerable individuals.
ab: Background

Adults with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) are at risk of requiring intensive care unit (ICU)-level care following allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT). Risk factors for admission to the ICU and outcomes are, however, poorly defined.
Objective

To assess risk factors associated with ICU admission in such patients, identify variables associated with ICU mortality, and analyze the outcome of ICU survivors in comparison to HCT recipients not admitted to the ICU.
Study Design
Here, we retrospectively analyzed a cohort of 1,265 adults with MDS/AML or AML who received an allograft while in first or second remission between 2006 and 2023.
Results

The cumulative incidence of ICU admission was 9.2% on day +100 after HCT. HCT-comorbidity index (hazard ratio [HR]=1.15, P=0.005), treatment-related mortality (TRM) score (HR=1.07, P=0.004), and graft from an HLA-mismatched donor (HR=2.19, P=0.018) were independently associated with ICU admission. Within 100 days of ICU admission, 50 patients (43%) died; poor performance status (odds ratio [OR]=5.45, P=0.005), higher TRM score (OR per one unit increase=1.14, P=0.035), and secondary AML (OR=2.71 P=0.035) were associated with increased day +100 mortality after ICU admission. In a landmark analysis, patients admitted to the ICU during the first 100 days after HCT and alive at day +150 had significantly higher NRM (HR=2.36, P<0.001) after multivariable adjustment.
Conclusion

Together, these results highlight that ICU admission is common after allografting in adults with AML and is associated with high mortality. Identification of patients at increased risk may, ultimately, help develop possible preventive strategies and allow testing in particularly vulnerable individuals.

papers.t: Patient-tailored azacitidine, venetoclax and gilteritinib triplet therapy appear to improve tolerability while preserving encouraging clinical outcomes in FLT3-mutated relapsed/refractory AML
papers.c: Median EFS was 40.5 months in Group 1 and was not reached at five years in Group 2, compared with 11.5 months in Group 3. Our data suggest that reducing the duration of triple-drug overlap may improve tolerability without compromising clinical outcomes.
ab: FLT3-mutated acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is associated with high relapse rates and treatment resistance. Triplet therapy with azacitidine (AZA), venetoclax (VEN), and the FLT3 inhibitor gilteritinib (GILT) yields high response rates but is limited by myelosuppression and infections. We conducted a multicenter retrospective study of 29 FLT3-mutated AML patients treated with GILT-triplets. The primary endpoint was overall survival (OS); secondary endpoints event-free survival (EFS) and time to neutrophil and platelet recovery. Patients received one of three regimens: concomitant triplet therapy (Group 1); concomitant AZA + VEN followed by concomitant VEN+GILT (Group 2); or overlapping AZA + VEN followed by GILT monotherapy (Group 3). For the entire cohort median OS was not reached after more than five years of follow-up. High response rates were observed across all schedules. Limiting concomitant exposure reduced myelosuppression and decreased infectious complications compared with full triplet therapy. Median OS was not reached in Groups 1 and 2 after three years, whereas Group 3 had a median OS of 18 months. Median EFS was 40.5 months in Group 1 and was not reached at five years in Group 2, compared with 11.5 months in Group 3. Our data suggest that reducing the duration of triple-drug overlap may improve tolerability without compromising clinical outcomes.

papers.t: High METTL16 expression is associated with inferior overall survival and transcriptional features of primitive cellular states in acute myeloid leukaemia
Patient-specific genomic measurable residual disease markers for monitoring acute myeloid leukaemia and myeloid malignancy
papers.c: Two patients with isolated CNS relapse had low-level BM involvement at extra-medullary relapse. Myeloid malignancy PCR-MRD should be studied prospectively in clinical trials across experienced MRD laboratories using the standardised EuroMRD guidelines.
ab: Measurable residual disease (MRD) has improved acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (ALL) outcomes. Applying acute myeloid leukaemia (AML) MRD has been limited due to complexity identifying leukaemia-specific targets. Current AML MRD relies on flow cytometry or ribonucleic acid (RNA)-based quantitative polymerase chain reaction (PCR) but cannot be applied to all patients. With next-generation or whole genome sequencing (NGS/WGS), myeloid MRD targets can be identified, suggesting that DNA-based PCR-MRD could be used. Genomic data including RNA-seq, targeted NGS or WGS were used to develop patient-specific PCR-MRD assays, which were reported using EuroMRD guidelines. We developed PCR-MRD assays in 97.6% patients and conducted prospective PCR-MRD monitoring in 40 myeloid malignancy patients. Myeloid MRD reports had a similar turnaround time to ALL MRD. Myeloid MRD markers were highly sensitive with a higher proportion of myeloid malignancy patients (50%) having an MRD marker with a quantitative range of ≤5 × 10-5 compared to ALL patients (29%). In patients with two MRD markers, there was excellent inter-assay concordance. Serial MRD correlated with disease outcome. Two patients with isolated CNS relapse had low-level BM involvement at extra-medullary relapse. Myeloid malignancy PCR-MRD should be studied prospectively in clinical trials across experienced MRD laboratories using the standardised EuroMRD guidelines.

papers.t: A rare case of acute basophilic leukemia transformed from high risk myelodysplastic syndrome
papers.c: The patient was treated with azacitidine and venetoclax, followed by best supportive care after disease progression. This case highlights the rare occurrence of ABL secondary to MDS and provides insight into the diagnostic challenges, clonal evolution, and therapeutic limitations associated with this aggressive entity.
ab: Acute basophilic leukemia (ABL) transformed from myelodysplastic syndrome is exceedingly rare. We report the case of a 73-year-old man with ABL which transformed from IPSS-M High risk MDS. The patient had a history of metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer. Further investigations demonstrated circulating blasts on peripheral blood smear. Upon bone marrow examination, a diagnosis of ABL arising from underlying MDS was established, characterized by cytogenetic analysis demonstrating trisomy 8 (+ 8), with the additional copy of chromosome 8 present in the form of a ring chromosome, and a WT1 frameshift mutation. The patient was treated with azacitidine and venetoclax, followed by best supportive care after disease progression. This case highlights the rare occurrence of ABL secondary to MDS and provides insight into the diagnostic challenges, clonal evolution, and therapeutic limitations associated with this aggressive entity.

papers.t: Targeting the mitochondrial complex I subunit NDUFS2 potentiates FLT3 inhibition in acute myeloid leukaemia with FLT3 internal tandem duplication
papers.c: A preliminary murine safety assessment showed no overt toxicity under the tested short-term dosing schedule. These findings identify NDUFS2-dependent complex I activity as an adaptive metabolic dependency supporting FLT3 inhibitor tolerance and provide mechanistic insight for further preclinical evaluation.
ab: Acute myeloid leukaemia (AML) with FLT3 internal tandem duplication (FLT3-ITD) frequently relapses after FLT3 tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy, highlighting the need to define mechanisms of drug tolerance. Here, we identify the mitochondrial complex I core subunit NDUFS2 as a determinant of FLT3 TKI tolerance in FLT3-ITD AML. A metabolism-focused CRISPR-Cas9 sensitiser screen, integrated with transcriptomic profiling of gilteritinib-resistant cells and primary samples, identified NDUFS2 as upregulated in acquired resistance and preferentially expressed in FLT3-ITD AML. NDUFS2 knockdown impaired complex I activity, oxidative phosphorylation, mitochondrial membrane potential and ATP production, thereby promoting apoptosis and sensitising FLT3-ITD AML cells to gilteritinib. Pharmacologic complex I inhibition with IACS-010759 similarly enhanced gilteritinib activity in FLT3-ITD AML cell lines and primary FLT3-ITD samples, activated AMPK-PERK-ATF4-CHOP stress signalling, promoted apoptosis, and reduced leukaemia burden in a patient-derived xenograft model. Genetic NDUFS2 knockdown also prolonged survival in a xenograft model. A preliminary murine safety assessment showed no overt toxicity under the tested short-term dosing schedule. These findings identify NDUFS2-dependent complex I activity as an adaptive metabolic dependency supporting FLT3 inhibitor tolerance and provide mechanistic insight for further preclinical evaluation.

papers.t: Ibrutinib and standard immunochemotherapy in younger, high-risk patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma: A phase II study of GLA
papers.c: In this prematurely closed phase II study, the addition of ibrutinib to R-CHOEP showed encouraging activity. However, findings remain exploratory and hypothesis generating only.
ab: Younger patients with high-risk diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) frequently have unfavourable outcomes. We conducted a prospective phase II study evaluating ibrutinib plus rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, prednisone (R-CHOEP+I) in patients aged 18-60 years with DLBCL and age-adjusted international prognostic index ≥2. Patients received ibrutinib (560 mg daily, d1-112) combined with eight cycles of R-CHOEP q2w. The primary end-point was 2-year progression-free survival (PFS). Outcomes were compared exploratorily with those of patients with identical inclusion criteria treated with R-CHOEP alone in the R-MegaCHOEP phase III trial (n = 130). Forty patients started R-CHOEP+I. Ibrutinib was administered for a median of 96 days, and 42% of patients completed treatment fully according to protocol. The overall response rate was 92%. Sixty-eight per cent received all R-CHOEP cycles compared with 88% in R-MegaCHOEP; 22% vs. 49% of patients with bulky and/or extranodal disease underwent radiotherapy. With a median follow-up of 31 months, 2-year PFS was 83% (95% CI, 71-95) vs. 75% (95% CI, 67-82) after R-CHOEP alone (p = 0.237). Exploratory cell-of-origin analyses suggested favourable outcomes in activated B-cell-type disease, but these findings remain descriptive. Grade ≥3 haematological adverse events were frequent, although no treatment-related deaths occurred. In this prematurely closed phase II study, the addition of ibrutinib to R-CHOEP showed encouraging activity. However, findings remain exploratory and hypothesis generating only.

papers.t: A multicentre phase III clinical trial of dual-epigenetic therapy plus CHOP compared with CHOP in previously untreated patients with peripheral T-cell lymphoma
papers.c: Although OS was longer in the AC-CHOP arm, this finding should be interpreted cautiously given the imbalances in post-protocol treatments between the two arms. Integration of molecular profiling may improve risk stratification and inform future biomarker-driven therapeutic strategies in PTCL.
ab: This phase 3 multicenter trial evaluated the efficacy and safety of adding dual epigenetic agents azacitidine and chidamide to CHOP (AC-CHOP) versus CHOP alone in previously untreated peripheral T-cell lymphoma (PTCL). A total of 128 patients were enrolled from 9 centers in China and assigned according to participating centers (AC-CHOP, N = 84; CHOP, N = 44). Azacitidine 200 mg on days 1-2, 100 mg on day 3 and chidamide 20 mg twice weekly were administered in the AC-CHOP arm. The AC-CHOP arm showed numerically higher ORR (60.7% vs. 54.6%) and CR rate (47.6% vs. 36.4%) than the CHOP arm, although the differences were not statistically significant. A trend toward improved PFS was observed in the AC-CHOP arm (median 10.2 months in the AC-CHOP arm vs. 8.4 months in the CHOP arm, P = 0.093), alongside a significantly improved OS (median 46.2 months vs. 24.1 months, P = 0.023). The safety profile was comparable between the two groups, with hematologic toxicity and infection being the most common adverse events. Genomic profiling showed that DNMT3A mutations were associated with lower response rates, while IDH2 and TP53 mutations were associated with inferior survival outcomes. In conclusion, the addition of chidamide and azacitidine to CHOP did not significantly improve ORR or PFS. Although OS was longer in the AC-CHOP arm, this finding should be interpreted cautiously given the imbalances in post-protocol treatments between the two arms. Integration of molecular profiling may improve risk stratification and inform future biomarker-driven therapeutic strategies in PTCL.

papers.t: Nirmatrelvir/Ritonavir and Subsequent PCR Negativity in Patients With B-Cell Lymphoma and Prolonged SARS-CoV-2 PCR Positivity: A Case Series
papers.c: Three patients received nirmatrelvir/ritonavir and became PCR negative 5-14 days after treatment initiation. These findings suggest that prolonged SARS-CoV-2 PCR positivity may disrupt lymphoma treatment and that PCR negativity was observed shortly after nirmatrelvir/ritonavir treatment in selected patients.
ab: Prolonged SARS-CoV-2 PCR positivity is increasingly recognized in immunocompromised patients. We retrospectively analyzed four patients with B-cell lymphoma and prior anti-CD20 antibody therapy who exhibited prolonged PCR positivity after COVID-19 diagnosis. The median duration of PCR positivity was 57 days (range, 47-78 days); lymphoma treatment was interrupted in one patient and could not be resumed in another. Three patients received nirmatrelvir/ritonavir and became PCR negative 5-14 days after treatment initiation. These findings suggest that prolonged SARS-CoV-2 PCR positivity may disrupt lymphoma treatment and that PCR negativity was observed shortly after nirmatrelvir/ritonavir treatment in selected patients.

papers.t: Adjusted Indirect Comparison Between Epcoritamab-R2 and Tafasitamab-R2 in Relapse/Refractory Follicular Lymphoma
papers.c: Finally, this is not a direct comparison of two therapeutic regimens and the results should be cautiously interpreted. Treatment choice should be decided on a case-by-case scenario based on several different variables.
ab: Treatment of relapsed refractory follicular lymphoma (R/R FL) still remains challenging. Several strategies have been used against R/R FL. Recently, two chemotherapy-free regimens have gained space, epcoritamab-lenalidomide-rituximab (Epco-R2) and tafasitamab-lenalidomide-rituximab (Tafa-R2). Herein, we performed an indirect trial comparison (ITC) between the two regimens using the Bucher method as they both have the common comparator arm R2. The ITC between the two study arms showed an overall response rate (ORR; p = 0.020), and complete remission rates (CR; p < 0.0001), in favor of Epco-R2. Analysis regarding time to next treatment (TTNT) interval also favored Epco-R2 (p = 0.0011). The ITC in the progression free survival (PFS) context showed the anchored comparison favored Epco-R2 over Tafa-R2 [HR 0.51 (95% CI 0.31-0.86)], p = 0.011, a finding more pronounced in patients with progression of disease within 24 months (POD24) negativity. Regarding the safety profile, Epco-R2 was associated with more hematological toxicity and infections, whereas, Tafa-R2 was associated with more COVID-19 infections probably reflecting the pandemic era enrollment timing. In conclusion, Epco-R2 is more effective in terms of treatment outcomes, but comes with greater toxicity. Tafa-R2 seems more suitable for patients with limited bone marrow reserves, patients who wish to avoid hospitalization, patients at a higher risk for cytokine release syndrome, and patients with high-risk infection vulnerability. Finally, this is not a direct comparison of two therapeutic regimens and the results should be cautiously interpreted. Treatment choice should be decided on a case-by-case scenario based on several different variables.

papers.t: Whole-genome and transcriptome analysis in relapsed/refractory non-Hodgkin lymphoma: Results from a multicentre precision oncology cohort
papers.c: Mutational signature analysis identified hypermutation patterns consistent with genomic damage associated with prior cytotoxic therapies. While our findings support the integration of WGTA into the care of patients with R/R lymphomas and identify opportunities for sequence-guided treatment, drug access, systematic barriers and delayed timing of testing currently limit clinical uptake and the potential of precision oncology in lymphoid malignancies.
ab: Comprehensive genome and transcriptome profiling can inform the diagnosis, prognosis and management of relapsed/refractory (R/R) solid malignancies, yet its integration into clinical care has lagged despite strong biological rationale. We evaluated the clinical utility of whole genome and transcriptome analysis (WGTA) in 65 patients (37 paediatric, 14 adolescents and young adults, 14 adults) with R/R non-Hodgkin lymphomas enrolled in Canadian precision oncology initiatives (Personalized Oncogenomics, Precision Oncology for Young People, Personalized Targeted Therapy in Refractory or Relapsed Cancer in Childhood, SickKids' Cancer Sequencing). WGTA provided clinically potentially useful findings in 89% of patients including therapy selection, diagnostic clarification, prediction of resistance, minimal residual disease marker identification and discovery of germline cancer predisposition. Results altered management in 15% of patients. Barriers to implementation included clinical deterioration, availability of standard therapies reducing the need for sequence-informed therapies and limited access to targeted agents. Transcriptome-based clustering delineated five biologically distinct subgroups independent of age or histological subtype with convergent oncogenic pathways. Mutational signature analysis identified hypermutation patterns consistent with genomic damage associated with prior cytotoxic therapies. While our findings support the integration of WGTA into the care of patients with R/R lymphomas and identify opportunities for sequence-guided treatment, drug access, systematic barriers and delayed timing of testing currently limit clinical uptake and the potential of precision oncology in lymphoid malignancies.

papers.t: Extracavitary Primary Effusion Lymphoma in an HIV-Negative Patient With Aberrant Immunophenotypic Features
Determinants of response to CAR T cell therapy in a multicenter, multi-trial cohort analysis of patients with lymphoma
papers.c: Mass cytometry by time-of-flight analysis of products from a subgroup of 116 patients confirmed an association between a CD8 naive-like T cell phenotype lacking expression of exhaustion markers, such as TIGIT, LAG-3 and PD-1, and PFS. The evidence generated by this study has the potential to advance the development of more effective cellular therapies.
ab: In patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) treated with chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy, factors associated with efficacy overlap with prognostic biomarkers. Currently, there is no consensus on optimal product characteristics. We analyzed the phenotypic attributes of the anti-CD19 CAR T therapy axicabtagene ciloleucel (axi-cel) from 580 patients with NHL across multiple clinical trials with long-term follow-up (median, 41.9 months). A high proportion of naive-like (CCR7+CD45RA+) T cells was the most significant feature associated with prolonged progression-free survival (PFS; hazard ratio = 0.46, 95% confidence interval: 0.31-0.68, P = 9.8 × 10-5, high versus low naive-like T cell groups) without impacting safety. The relationship between naive-like T cells and efficacy was independent of tumor microenvironment characteristics (assessed in 112 patients). In multivariate models, the naive-like phenotype outperformed clinicopathologic features such as inflammatory markers and tumor burden, remaining significant after adjusting for product expansion. An inverse correlation was observed between prior lines of therapy and the proportion of naive-like T cells in both product and matched apheresis samples, suggesting a benefit of earlier intervention. The key findings were validated in an independent cohort of 203 patients treated with axi-cel-based therapy or brexucabtagene autoleucel. Mass cytometry by time-of-flight analysis of products from a subgroup of 116 patients confirmed an association between a CD8 naive-like T cell phenotype lacking expression of exhaustion markers, such as TIGIT, LAG-3 and PD-1, and PFS. The evidence generated by this study has the potential to advance the development of more effective cellular therapies.

papers.t: Frontline Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitors are associated with improved response and PFS in primary CNS lymphoma
papers.c: The overall survival difference was not statistically significant (HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.31-1.38; P=0.263), which may reflect multifactorial confounding inherent in this retrospective comparison. These findings suggest that integrating BTKi into frontline regimens is associated with a favorable PFS profile and improved response in newly diagnosed PCNSL, while definitive OS conclusions cannot be drawn.
ab: High-dose methotrexate (HD-MTX)-based immunochemotherapy remains the standard for primary CNS lymphoma (PCNSL), yet relapse rates are high and outcomes suboptimal. While Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitors (BTKi) demonstrate efficacy in trials, their comparative benefit against conventional regimens in heterogeneous real-world populations remains undefined. We conducted a retrospective study of 131 newly diagnosed patients stratified by frontline induction therapy (BTKi-based, n=85; conventional, n=46), utilizing multiple imputation (m=50) and inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) to balance baseline covariates. In the primary pooled multiple-imputation IPTW analysis, BTKi-based therapy was associated with improved PFS (HR 0.57, 95% CI 0.32-1.00; P=0.048) and a higher complete response rate (OR 5.50, 95% CI 2.25-13.47; P<0.001). The objective response rate was also higher (OR 2.59, 95% CI 1.05-6.36; P=0.038). The overall survival difference was not statistically significant (HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.31-1.38; P=0.263), which may reflect multifactorial confounding inherent in this retrospective comparison. These findings suggest that integrating BTKi into frontline regimens is associated with a favorable PFS profile and improved response in newly diagnosed PCNSL, while definitive OS conclusions cannot be drawn.

papers.t: Outcomes of gastrointestinal bleeding events after first-line chemotherapy in gastrointestinal-diffuse large B-cell lymphoma: a propensity-score matched analysis
papers.c: GIB was successfully managed with conservative medical therapy in the majority of cases (77.78%), with the remainder (22.22%) requiring endoscopic hemostasis. Post-chemotherapy GIB in GI-DLBCL is associated with a poor prognosis, particularly in patients with elevated baseline PET/CT metabolic parameters indicative of high tumor burden.
ab: Gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB) is a life-threatening complication of first-line chemotherapy in gastrointestinal diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (GI-DLBCL), yet its prognostic significance remains poorly defined. This propensity score-matched study (1:2) included 79 patients with GI-DLBCL, comparing 9 with post-chemotherapy GIB to controls without GIB. Matching was based on gender, clinical stage, Hans classification, and Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status. Patients with GIB had worse overall survival (OS, P = 0.006) and progression-free survival(PFS, P = 0.011), with markedly lower complete (11.11% vs. 66.67%, P = 0.013) and objective (66.67% vs. 100.00%, P = 0.029) response rates. Higher baseline PET-CT parameters including gastrointestinal-metabolic tumor volume (GI-MTV, P = 0.002) and gastrointestinal-total lesion glycolysis (GI-TLG, P = 0.004) indicated GIB occurrence. In the survival analysis, high ECOG (P = 0.032), whole-body metabolic tumor volume (Wb-MTV, P = 0.012), and total lesion glycolysis (Wb-TLG, P = 0.038) might be associated with poor OS, while high ECOG (P = 0.008) and international prognostic index (IPI, P =0.027) were associated with poor PFS. GIB was successfully managed with conservative medical therapy in the majority of cases (77.78%), with the remainder (22.22%) requiring endoscopic hemostasis. Post-chemotherapy GIB in GI-DLBCL is associated with a poor prognosis, particularly in patients with elevated baseline PET/CT metabolic parameters indicative of high tumor burden.

papers.t: MTHFR C677T genetic polymorphisms are not a decisive factor in delayed methotrexate excretion in central nervous system lymphoma patients
papers.c: Our findings demonstrate that urine acidification and hypoalbuminemia, rather than MTHFR C677T polymorphism, constitute primary risk factors for HD-MTX excretion delay in treatment cycles. These results suggest that optimal management should prioritize urinary alkalinization (pH ≥ 7.0) and albumin level maintenance over genotype-guided dose reduction. These modifiable factors present actionable targets for improving HD-MTX safety profiles in CNS lymphoma treatment.
ab: Background

High-dose methotrexate (HD-MTX) serves as a cornerstone treatment for central nervous system lymphoma. However, its clinical utility is limited by delayed drug excretion and associated adverse events. The methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) C677T polymorphism, a critical genetic variant influencing MTX metabolism, has been proposed by some experts as an indicator for HD-MTX dose reduction due to its potential association with delayed excretion.
Objective
This study aimed to identify clinical risk factors for delayed MTX excretion and evaluate the predictive value of MTHFR C677T polymorphism in HD-MTX treatment cycles for CNS lymphoma patients.
Methods

We conducted a retrospective analysis of 213 HD-MTX treatment cycles in CNS lymphoma patients (derived from 98 patients) treated at our institution between May 2015 and December 2023. Each patient received a median of 3 HD-MTX cycles (range 1-9 cycles). Treatment cycles were stratified into delayed excretion (n = 66) and normal excretion (n = 147) groups based on international consensus guidelines for pharmacokinetic monitoring of serum MTX concentrations. MTHFR C677T genotypes were analyzed using PCR-RFLP with Sanger sequencing validation (10% random sample). Clinical parameters were compared between groups; univariate logistic regression (retention threshold: P < 0.10) was used for initial risk factor screening, and a mixed-effects logistic regression model with a random intercept for individual patients (retention: P < 0.05) was applied for identifying independent risk factors to correct for non-independence of repeated measures.
Results

Univariate analysis revealed four potential risk factors (P < 0.1): advanced age (OR = 1.03), MTHFR C677T CT/TT (OR = 1.73), hypoalbuminemia (< 35 g/L) (OR = 3.42), and acidic urine pH (< 7.0) (OR = 4.15). Mixed-effects multivariate analysis identified hypoalbuminemia (adjusted OR = 3.02, 95%CI 1.56-5.85) and acidic urine pH (adjusted OR = 4.15, 95%CI 2.17-7.94) as independent predictors of delayed excretion (P < 0.05), with a random effect variance of σ²=0.21 indicating mild individual intervariability. The MTHFR C677T CT/TT genotype showed no statistically significant association in the adjusted model (P = 0.095). A total of 35.1% (13/37) of patients with CT/TT genotype exhibited delayed clearance in initial cycles (1-2) but normalized excretion in subsequent administrations (cycles 3-6, involving 42 treatment cycles). The median number of HD-MTX cycles administered was 4 (range 1-8) in patients with at least one delayed excretion cycle and 5 (range 1-9) in patients with all normal excretion cycles.
Conclusion

Our findings demonstrate that urine acidification and hypoalbuminemia, rather than MTHFR C677T polymorphism, constitute primary risk factors for HD-MTX excretion delay in treatment cycles. These results suggest that optimal management should prioritize urinary alkalinization (pH ≥ 7.0) and albumin level maintenance over genotype-guided dose reduction. These modifiable factors present actionable targets for improving HD-MTX safety profiles in CNS lymphoma treatment.

papers.t: N-AVD or BrECADD for Advanced-Stage Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma: Choosing the Right Treatment for the Right Patient
papers.c: The relevant trade-offs differ: hematologic and infectious toxicity, immune-related adverse events, fertility, long-term toxicity, radiotherapy exposure, PET availability, and health-system logistics may each influence regimen selection. Rather than identifying a universal winner, contemporary practice should define which patient is best suited to each strategy and incorporate shared decision-making into frontline treatment.
ab: Frontline therapy for advanced-stage classical Hodgkin lymphoma (cHL) has entered a new era. Two phase III trials have established highly effective but conceptually different strategies: nivolumab plus doxorubicin, vinblastine, and dacarbazine (N-AVD) in SWOG S1826 and PET-adapted BrECADD in GHSG HD21. Because these regimens were tested against different comparators and in different populations, their outcomes should not be interpreted as a head-to-head comparison. This review focuses on translating both trials into individualized treatment selection. N-AVD combines excellent disease control with relatively low hematologic toxicity, minimal use of radiotherapy, operational simplicity, and direct evidence across a broad age range, including patients older than 60 years. BrECADD provides mature disease-control data, PET2-guided treatment duration, potentially only 4 cycles in patients with complete metabolic response, lower anthracycline exposure in PET2-negative patients, and substantially improved gonadal recovery compared with eBEACOPP. The relevant trade-offs differ: hematologic and infectious toxicity, immune-related adverse events, fertility, long-term toxicity, radiotherapy exposure, PET availability, and health-system logistics may each influence regimen selection. Rather than identifying a universal winner, contemporary practice should define which patient is best suited to each strategy and incorporate shared decision-making into frontline treatment.

papers.t: Maintenance ALK inhibitor after hematopoietic cell transplantation in patients with anaplastic large cell lymphoma
Mogamulizumab efficacy on the skin compartment of cutaneous T-cell lymphomas based on longitudinal analysis
papers.c: Actual values of mSWAT scores decreased for responders at Week (W) 12 and 24 from baseline (BL) (mean ± standard error: BL: 97.57 ± 6.52; W12: 52.34 ± 6.16; W24: 34.89 ± 4.93) following a rapid decrease of CD7- cells in blood at W4 (BL: 2809 ± 650.3/μL; W4: 204.4 ± 50.76/μL; W12: 101.9 ± 28.81/μL; W24: 152.8 ± 54.98/μL). Monitoring both blood and skin improvements is important for effective mogamulizumab treatment in patients with advanced stage disease.
ab: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma is staged by the degree of skin, lymph node, viscera and blood involvement. Skin response is a determinant of treatment decisions. Mogamulizumab, an anti-CC chemokine receptor 4 antibody, is approved for mycosis fungoides and Sézary syndrome after ≥1 systemic therapy. Longitudinal changes in modified Severity-Weighted Assessment Tool (mSWAT) score, and cluster of differentiation (CD)4+CD7-/CD26- cell subsets during mogamulizumab treatment were investigated as an exploratory post-hoc analysis. While chronological differences in mSWAT scores were not interpreted by a linear mixed model (LMM) due to a statistically significant interaction term, significant differences based on responses in CD7- (-690.5/μL; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1195 to -186.2; p = 0.0076) and CD26- (-1029/μL; 95% CI, -1705 to -353.7; p = 0.0030) cell counts were identified. Actual values of mSWAT scores decreased for responders at Week (W) 12 and 24 from baseline (BL) (mean ± standard error: BL: 97.57 ± 6.52; W12: 52.34 ± 6.16; W24: 34.89 ± 4.93) following a rapid decrease of CD7- cells in blood at W4 (BL: 2809 ± 650.3/μL; W4: 204.4 ± 50.76/μL; W12: 101.9 ± 28.81/μL; W24: 152.8 ± 54.98/μL). Monitoring both blood and skin improvements is important for effective mogamulizumab treatment in patients with advanced stage disease.

papers.t: CAR-HEMATOTOX score to predict risk of poor outcomes with odronextamab in heavily pretreated B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma
papers.c: In patients with HThigh versus HTlow scores, progression-free survival (PFS) was significantly poorer in DLBCL (2.6 vs. 9.6 months [p < 0.0001]), and overall survival (OS) was significantly worse in FL and DLBCL (FL, 26.5 months vs. not reached [p = 0.030]; DLBCL, 4.8 vs. 17.2 months [p < 0.0001]). These results suggest that the CAR-HEMATOTOX score may provide a readily available measure for identifying patients at risk of inferior clinical outcomes with odronextamab treatment.
ab: The CAR-HEMATOTOX model has been shown to help identify patients with relapsed/refractory (R/R) large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL) at heightened risk of severe neutropenia, serious infection and worse clinical outcomes after chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy. We evaluated whether CAR-HEMATOTOX scores had prognostic value in patients with R/R follicular lymphoma (FL) or diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) treated with odronextamab (cluster of differentiation [CD]20 × CD3 bispecific antibody) in the ELM-1 (NCT02290951) and ELM-2 (NCT03888105) studies. Patients were retrospectively stratified by baseline CAR-HEMATOTOX score: CAR-HEMATOTOX score low (HTlow [0-1]; FL, n = 115, DLBCL, n = 92) or CAR-HEMATOTOX score high (HThigh [≥2]; FL, n = 24, DLBCL, n = 98). The incidence of grade ≥2 cytokine release syndrome within the first 30 treatment days, and rates of grade ≥3 infection and delayed neutrophil recovery within the first 90 treatment days, were numerically higher in HThigh versus HTlow patients. In patients with HThigh versus HTlow scores, progression-free survival (PFS) was significantly poorer in DLBCL (2.6 vs. 9.6 months [p < 0.0001]), and overall survival (OS) was significantly worse in FL and DLBCL (FL, 26.5 months vs. not reached [p = 0.030]; DLBCL, 4.8 vs. 17.2 months [p < 0.0001]). These results suggest that the CAR-HEMATOTOX score may provide a readily available measure for identifying patients at risk of inferior clinical outcomes with odronextamab treatment.

papers.t: Predictors and Outcomes of Immune Effector Cell Associated Neurotoxicity Syndrome in Patients Receiving Chimeric Antigen Receptor T Cell Therapy for Aggressive B-Cell Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma
papers.c: Evaluation of the EASIX and m-EASIX scores in our data set demonstrated limited discriminatory ability in predicting development of ICANS (AUC 0.64 and 0.66 respectively). Additionally, CRP alone performed similarly to these scores (AUC 0.64), highlighting the need for novel predictive models for severe ICANS which might aid in appropriate product selection and lead to strategies to prevent neurologic toxicity after CAR-T treatment.
ab: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy has revolutionized the treatment for patients with aggressive relapsed or refractory B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (B-NHL). One notable complication is immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) which can be life-threatening. Treatment includes supportive care along with corticosteroids, often for protracted time periods. While ICANS presentation can be variable, it was previously unknown whether patients experiencing ICANS and treated with steroids had reduced CAR-T cell activity and worse outcomes. In addition, the optimal predictors of severe ICANS prior to lymphodepletion remain incompletely understood with a few studies suggesting utility of the endothelial stress activation index (EASIX) score or the modified EASIX score (m-EASIX). We conducted a multicenter retrospective analysis of 352 patients who received axicabtagene ciloleucel (axi-cel) or tisagenlecleucel (tisa-cel) for the treatment of B-NHL. In this cohort 125 patients developed ICANS (35.5%). Survival was not different among patients who did not develop ICANS, with median PFS of 4.1 months (vs 9.5 months in those who developed ICANS, P = 0.37) and median OS in patients who did not develop ICANS was 25.3 (vs 15.2 months in those who developed ICANS, P = 0.16). Evaluation of the EASIX and m-EASIX scores in our data set demonstrated limited discriminatory ability in predicting development of ICANS (AUC 0.64 and 0.66 respectively). Additionally, CRP alone performed similarly to these scores (AUC 0.64), highlighting the need for novel predictive models for severe ICANS which might aid in appropriate product selection and lead to strategies to prevent neurologic toxicity after CAR-T treatment.

papers.t: Glofitamab with polatuzumab vedotin in relapsed/refractory central nervous system lymphomas
papers.c: These data indicate glofitamab with polatuzumab vedotin is capable of safely inducing deep and rapid clinical remissions in r/r CNSL, including in high-risk histological and molecular subtypes. Future prospective evaluation of the regimen for r/r CNSL is warranted given the unmet need of this population.
ab: Patients with relapsed/refractory (r/r) central nervous system lymphoma (CNSL) have poor survival with currently available treatments. Early reports suggest antibody-based treatments such as bispecific antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates can penetrate the blood-brain barrier and induce clinical responses in r/r CNSL. In this study, we retrospectively evaluated the safety and activity of glofitamab plus polatuzumab vedotin in 9 r/r CNSL patients treated at our institution, including high-risk subtypes such as chemorefractory Burkitt lymphoma and TP53-mutant Mantle cell lymphoma. Here, we observed a 100% overall and 89% complete response rate. Responses occurred in patients with brain parenchymal and leptomeningeal involvement, with rapid clearance of lymphoma cells from the cerebrospinal fluid within days of treatment as assessed by flow cytometry. Safety aligned with the known toxicity profile of the regimen in patients with systemic lymphomas. These data indicate glofitamab with polatuzumab vedotin is capable of safely inducing deep and rapid clinical remissions in r/r CNSL, including in high-risk histological and molecular subtypes. Future prospective evaluation of the regimen for r/r CNSL is warranted given the unmet need of this population.

papers.t: Newly diagnosed and relapsed follicular lymphoma: EHA Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up
papers.c: Patients should be actively involved in decision-making. In this guideline, we present current evidence-based recommendations for diagnosis, staging, treatment, and follow-up.
ab: Follicular lymphoma (FL) is the second most common lymphoma subtype in Europe, with a median age at diagnosis of 60-65 years. It is generally considered an indolent disease, and the median overall survival at diagnosis now likely exceeds 20 years. However, considerable heterogeneity exists. Diagnosis requires adequate biopsy material and a specialized hematopathologist. Staging and prognosis rely on positron emission tomography (PET)-computed tomography (CT). Prognostication at diagnosis is based on several validated clinical prognostic scores. Localized disease is usually treated with radiotherapy ± Rituximab. The treatment of disseminated disease includes active surveillance (or in selected cases Rituximab monotherapy) for low-tumor burden patients, and most often immunochemotherapy (or in selected cases chemo-free therapeutic options), ±antibody maintenance in high-tumor burden patients. For relapsed or refractory disease, treatment with Rituximab-Lenalidomide combination ± Tafasitamab or Epcoritamab from the first relapse and single-agent bispecific antibodies, chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy (CAR-T) cells, and Zanubrutinib-Obinutuzumab after second relapse should be prioritized over immunochemotherapy. Given the long natural history and risk of relapse, careful follow-up is an important part of patient management. Patients should be actively involved in decision-making. In this guideline, we present current evidence-based recommendations for diagnosis, staging, treatment, and follow-up.

papers.t: In a Nutshell: Immune alterations in classic Hodgkin lymphoma

Addition of thiotepa to total body irradiation-based conditioning in allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation for relapsed/refractory acute leukemia and lymphoma: a propensity score-matched retrospective study
papers.c: Adding thiotepa to TBI-based conditioning for R/R AL is associated with lower relapse incidence without compromising OS, DFS, engraftment, or GVHD, at the cost of increased mucosal toxicity. The relapse finding requires cautious interpretation and prospective validation.
ab: Background

Relapsed/refractory (R/R) acute leukemia (AL) carries a poor prognosis, with allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) the primary curative option. Total body irradiation (TBI)-based conditioning is a cornerstone, but optimizing intensity remains challenging. Thiotepa, a bifunctional alkylating agent, may enhance disease control when added to TBI, but data in R/R AL are lacking.
Methods

This single-center retrospective study (2020-2025) included R/R AL and lymphoma patients receiving TBI-based conditioning with (TBI + TT) or without (TBI) thiotepa. Propensity score matching (1:2, caliper = 0.2) used 9 covariates. Primary endpoints were overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS). Secondary endpoints included relapse, non-relapse mortality (NRM), engraftment, GVHD, CMV infection, and mucositis. Kaplan-Meier, Fine-Gray competing risk, and inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) analyses were employed.
Results

After matching, 48 TBI + TT and 86 TBI patients were analyzed. OS (HR = 0.901, 95% CI 0.569-1.425, P = 0.655) and DFS (HR = 0.809, 95% CI 0.504-1.299, P = 0.380) were comparable. The 1-year relapse cumulative incidence was lower with TBI + TT (6.7% vs. 17.8%, Gray's P = 0.035; multivariable sHR = 0.280, 95% CI 0.083-0.942, P = 0.040), though hypothesis-generating given only 3 relapse events. NRM was comparable (Gray's P = 0.374). Mucositis was significantly higher with TBI + TT (81.2% vs. 64.0%, P = 0.049). IPTW confirmed comparable OS (P = 0.690) and DFS (P = 0.975).
Conclusion

Adding thiotepa to TBI-based conditioning for R/R AL is associated with lower relapse incidence without compromising OS, DFS, engraftment, or GVHD, at the cost of increased mucosal toxicity. The relapse finding requires cautious interpretation and prospective validation.

papers.t: Ferritin and LDH predict thrombotic risk beyond conventional scoring systems in DLBCL
papers.c: In DLBCL, where no standardized thrombosis risk-stratification approach exists, elevated ferritin at diagnosis independently predicted thrombotic events, while LDH was significant in univariate analysis. These readily available parameters may contribute to lymphoma-specific thrombosis scoring systems and warrant prospective validation.
ab: Thrombotic events are clinically significant complications in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) that adversely affect treatment continuity and outcomes. Despite their importance, no standardized predictive approach exists, and traditional cancer-associated thrombosis models perform suboptimally in hematological malignancies. We retrospectively analyzed 133 adult patients with DLBCL treated at a single center between 2009 and 2021. Thrombotic events required objective radiological confirmation. Baseline demographic, clinical, and laboratory parameters were compared between patients with and without thrombosis. ROC analysis determined the optimal ferritin cutoff, and Cox proportional hazards and Fine-Gray competing-risk models (with death as a competing event) identified independent predictors. Thrombosis occurred in 16 patients (12.0%), all venous. Baseline clinical characteristics and the Khorana score did not differ between groups. Patients with thrombosis had significantly higher ferritin (median 331.5 vs. 113 ng/mL; p = 0.026) and LDH (median 459.5 vs. 256 U/L; p = 0.022). ROC analysis identified a ferritin cutoff of ≥ 227 ng/mL (AUC 0.686, 95% CI 0.532-0.840), associated with a 6.1-fold increased risk (OR 6.10, 95% CI 1.75-21.28). In multivariate Cox regression, ferritin ≥ 227 ng/mL (HR 3.77, 95% CI 1.13-12.60, p = 0.031) was an independent predictor and remained significant in competing-risk analysis (sHR 4.68); LDH was significant in Cox analysis (HR 1.002 per unit increase, p = 0.034) but was attenuated in the competing-risk model. In DLBCL, where no standardized thrombosis risk-stratification approach exists, elevated ferritin at diagnosis independently predicted thrombotic events, while LDH was significant in univariate analysis. These readily available parameters may contribute to lymphoma-specific thrombosis scoring systems and warrant prospective validation.

papers.t: Treatment patterns and outcomes for second-line therapy in large B-cell lymphoma: results from the LEO CReWE study
papers.c: Patients intended for but unable to receive ASCT or CAR-T experienced poor outcomes comparable to those never intended for curative therapy at 2L. The LEO CReWE study represents the first large-scale depiction of 2L treatment patterns and outcomes for LBCL in the modern era, inclusive of all treatment approaches, and underscores the ongoing need for more effective therapies despite the advent of CAR-T.
ab: Treatment strategies for relapsed/refractory large B-cell lymphoma (R/R LBCL) have evolved rapidly, yet relationships between therapy selection and outcomes remain poorly defined. The LEO CReWE study evaluated disease characteristics, patterns of care, and outcomes in 1504 patients with R/R LBCL from 2002 to 2022. Of these, 64% received chemoimmunotherapy at second-line (2L). Autologous stem cell transplant (ASCT) and/or chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy (CAR-T) were planned at 2L for 984 patients (65%), with 471 (31%) ultimately receiving ASCT and 94 (6%) receiving CAR-T. Complete response (CR) rates at 2L ranged from 24% for lenalidomide-based regimens to 49% for CAR-T; salvage chemotherapy achieved a 44% CR rate overall and 60% among patients who eventually underwent ASCT. Median event-free and overall survival from 2L were 4.3 months and 18.3 months, respectively; survival improved in eras during which CAR-T was available. Patients intended for but unable to receive ASCT or CAR-T experienced poor outcomes comparable to those never intended for curative therapy at 2L. The LEO CReWE study represents the first large-scale depiction of 2L treatment patterns and outcomes for LBCL in the modern era, inclusive of all treatment approaches, and underscores the ongoing need for more effective therapies despite the advent of CAR-T.

papers.t: Late cardiopulmonary morbidity in patients with Hodgkin lymphoma: a retrospective nationwide registry study
papers.c: In conclusion, with the current treatment modalities, late cardiopulmonary morbidity in long-term survivors remains a great challenge. A strategy for primary prevention and early detection of late toxicity remains crucial and a critical evaluation of current treatment practices is warranted.
ab: Hodgkin lymphoma (HL) is a B-cell neoplasm with a cure rate of 90%. Previous data on late morbidity in patients with HL cover the era of older treatment modalities. This real-world study consisted of 2912 patients diagnosed with HL between 2000 and 2019 in Finland and aimed to clarify the incidence of late-onset cardiopulmonary morbidity compared to matched controls. Patient data were collected from four nationwide Finnish healthcare registries. We reported a higher occurrence of coronary artery disease in patients aged < 50 years at diagnosis than in controls (RR 3.80 (2.16-6.74), p < 0001). Additionally, a higher incidence of both heart failure (RR 1.68 (1.28-2.21), p < 0.001) and valvular heart disease (RR 1.80 (1.17-2.78), p = 0.006) was detected in patients aged ≥ 50 years at diagnosis than in the controls. Remarkably, in the < 50 years age group, the incidences of pneumonia (RR 4.89 (3.58-6.71), p < 0.001) and pulmonary embolism (RR 7.78 (2.75-21.95), p < 0.001) were higher than those in the control group. In conclusion, with the current treatment modalities, late cardiopulmonary morbidity in long-term survivors remains a great challenge. A strategy for primary prevention and early detection of late toxicity remains crucial and a critical evaluation of current treatment practices is warranted.

papers.t: Multiple myeloma in the Netherlands: 35-year trends in incidence and survival
Impact of extramedullary plasmacytoma on outcomes in patients with relapsed refractory multiple myeloma treated with talquetamab: U.S. Myeloma Immunotherapy Consortium
papers.c: These findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation. Talquetamab retains clinical utility in this high-risk population with EMD, though outcomes are suboptimal with a need for further refinement of treatment approaches.
ab: Talquetamab, a GPRC5D-targeting bispecific antibody, shows promising activity in relapsed-refractory multiple myeloma. However, real-world outcomes in patients with extramedullary disease (EMD) remain poorly described. We studied 360 patients treated with talquetamab at 15 U.S. centers by Dec 2024. Soft tissue plasmacytomas (STP) were classified as EMD (not contiguous with bone) or paraskeletal disease (PSD; contiguous with bone). If both were present, patients were assigned to the EMD category. Of those, 97 (27%) had EMD, 22 (6%) had PSD, and 241 (67%) had No-STP. Median follow-up was 12.8 months. Overall response rates were 68% in EMD, 63% in PSD, and 65% in No-STP (p = 0.8). Median progression-free survival was 4.3, 4.5, and 7.8 months, respectively (p = 0.009), and median overall survival was 10.3 months, 13.0 months, and not reached (p = 0.070). These findings demonstrate that EMD and PSD are associated with preserved response rates but shorter PFS and OS with talquetamab. While systemic markers of tumor burden and inflammation-particularly lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) and ferritin-emerged as independent predictors of inferior PFS, elevated LDH also retained independent prognostic significance for OS. While EMD was associated with shorter PFS and OS on univariate analysis, it did not retain independent prognostic significance on multivariable analysis, suggesting that inferior outcomes are driven by aggressive disease biology rather than by lesion anatomy alone. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation. Talquetamab retains clinical utility in this high-risk population with EMD, though outcomes are suboptimal with a need for further refinement of treatment approaches.

papers.t: Utilization of zoledronic acid and denosumab in patients with multiple myeloma: Real-world experience from 13 427 patients
APOBEC Status Classification Using a Curated Gene Panel in Multiple Myeloma
Allogeneic transplantation for plasma cell myeloma clears pre-transplant clonal haematopoiesis and is associated with a low rate of myeloid neoplasm post-cytotoxic-therapy
Integrated transcriptomics reveals a TNFRSF-metabolism axis and a context-dependent BCMA signaling state in myeloma progression
papers.c: When focusing specifically on BCMA, the prognostic ordering across BCMA x metabolism strata was not identical to the pooled TNFRSF model, underscoring that metabolic risk is modulated by the receptor state rather than acting as a universal driver. These findings define an integrated TNFRSF-metabolism axis and a context-dependent BCMA state in advanced MM, clinically relevant but adjustment-sensitive survival associations that warrant further validation and combination strategies that explicitly consider metabolic status.
ab: Multiple myeloma (MM) evolves from monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) and smoldering multiple myeloma (SMM) with extensive metabolic reprogramming and immune remodeling. We investigated whether coordinated activation of the tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily (TNFRSF) aligns with metabolic state and prognosis across this continuum. We integrated bone-marrow single-cell RNA sequencing from healthy donors, MGUS, SMM, and MM with bulk RNA sequencing from the Multiple Myeloma Research Foundation (MMRF) CoMMpass cohort. At single-cell resolution, per-cell metabolic activity scores increased with disease stage and were highest in malignant plasma cells. TNF/TNFRSF signaling was strongest in MM, and expression of TNFRSF17 (B-cell maturation antigen, BCMA) in plasma cells correlated with metabolic activity (Spearman ρ = 0.56 in MM). In the clinical cohort, a pooled TNFRSF score stratified overall survival (log-rank p < 0.0001), with individual associations for TNFRSF17 and TNFRSF1A/1B. Joint stratification by TNFRSF activation and metabolic activity revealed the poorest outcomes in tumors with low TNFRSF activation but high metabolic activity, indicating that metabolic state contributes to adverse risk in a receptor-context-dependent manner, while TNFRSF captured additional risk not explained by metabolism alone. When focusing specifically on BCMA, the prognostic ordering across BCMA x metabolism strata was not identical to the pooled TNFRSF model, underscoring that metabolic risk is modulated by the receptor state rather than acting as a universal driver. These findings define an integrated TNFRSF-metabolism axis and a context-dependent BCMA state in advanced MM, clinically relevant but adjustment-sensitive survival associations that warrant further validation and combination strategies that explicitly consider metabolic status.

papers.t: The EF1α promoter of cilta-cel drives a highly effective GZMK+ transcriptional program
papers.c: In myeloma xenograft models, the EF1α promoter in cilta-cel, rather than binding domain, recapitulated increased tumor control, enhanced expansion, and GZMK transcriptional profile compared with the MND promoter (ide-cel). These findings suggest that the efficacy of cilta-cel is linked to an EF1α-driven GZMK⁺ transcriptional trajectory that supports both persistence and effector function.
ab: Ciltacabtagene autoleucel (cilta-cel) and idecabtagene vicleucel (ide-cel) are approved BCMA-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells approved for the treatment of multiple myeloma. Although the higher efficacy of cilta-cel compared to ide-cel may be related to its unique nanobody binding domain, the constructs also differ in their use of EF1α and MND promoters, respectively, to drive CAR expression. To elucidate the basis of cilta-cel's efficacy, we analyzed CAR T cells from 87 patients with multiple myeloma (50 cilta-cel, 37 ide-cel) using flow cytometry and single-cell multi-omics. Cilta-cel showed a 10- fold higher peak expansion and greater persistence, driven by an inflammatory GZMK⁺ T cell subset marked by EOMES expression and motif accessibility, but not exhaustion profile. In myeloma xenograft models, the EF1α promoter in cilta-cel, rather than binding domain, recapitulated increased tumor control, enhanced expansion, and GZMK transcriptional profile compared with the MND promoter (ide-cel). These findings suggest that the efficacy of cilta-cel is linked to an EF1α-driven GZMK⁺ transcriptional trajectory that supports both persistence and effector function.

papers.t: Molecular predictors of minimal residual disease in newly diagnosed multiple myeloma treated with quadruplet therapy
papers.c: These findings define a multiomic classification of NDMM linked to Isa-KRd response. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04934475 .
ab: Quadruplet therapy, combining anti-CD38 antibodies, immunomodulatory drugs, proteasome inhibitors and dexamethasone, is now the standard induction treatment for newly diagnosed multiple myeloma (NDMM). However, treatment response is heterogeneous and molecular predictors are needed to guide early therapeutic decisions. We performed integrated genomic, transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling of 423 tumor samples from patients with NDMM from the MIDAS cohort to characterize molecular heterogeneity and its association with measurable residual disease (MRD) after quadruplet induction with isatuximab, carfilzomib, lenalidomide and dexamethasone (Isa-KRd). Postinduction MRD-negativity rates varied significantly across gene expression subtypes, with HP1/HP3 and MS groups showing superior responses compared to the MF and CD2 subtypes. B cell differentiation was associated with MRD positivity, while proliferation and MYC programs were associated with MRD negativity. These MRD-associated transcriptomic features were independently validated in the CASSIOPEIA cohort. Whole-genome sequencing revealed both known (APOBEC mutagenesis, chromothripsis) and new genomic instability phenotypes validated in the MMRF cohort. New driver alterations were identified with independent validation across three external cohorts with multiple myeloma (MMRF, MANHATTAN and CASSIOPEIA; 1,451 cases). Genomic instability features and driver genes such as CCND1 and MYC correlated with differential MRD outcomes. DNA methylation profiling identified nine MRD-linked subgroups distinguished by the extent of hypomethylation in quiescent chromatin and cis/trans signatures of driver translocations. A multimodal random forest model integrating genomic, transcriptomic and epigenomic features predicted MRD status after induction, with an area under the curve of 0.77, outperforming clinical and genomic models, while providing comparable discrimination and improved calibration relative to the transcriptomic and epigenomic models. These findings define a multiomic classification of NDMM linked to Isa-KRd response. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04934475 .
